items.value: The Supreme Court has located the Right to Privacy in Article 21
items.reasoning: In K. S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017) a nine-judge bench held that the right to privacy is protected as an intrinsic part of the right to life and personal liberty guaranteed by Article 21, and as a part of the freedoms guaranteed by Part III generally. Article 21 is therefore the anchoring provision. Articles 15 and 16 deal with non-discrimination and equality of opportunity in public employment, and Article 19 with the specified freedoms such as speech and movement — privacy draws support from Article 19 only derivatively, whereas its home is Article 21.

items.value: Statements 1 and 3 only — the CDS is Permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee and Principal Military Adviser to the Defence Minister, but exercises no military command over the Service Chiefs
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: the Chief of Defence Staff is the Permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee. Statement 3 is correct: he is the Principal Military Adviser to the Raksha Mantri on all tri-Service matters, while the three Service Chiefs continue to advise the Minister on matters exclusively concerning their own Services. Statement 2 is expressly excluded by the terms on which the post was created — the CDS will not exercise any military command, including over the three Service Chiefs, so as to be able to render impartial advice. With 2 out and both 1 and 3 in, only the combination 1 and 3 survives.

items.value: Operation Sadbhavana is the Army's welfare and development outreach to local populations in remote areas
items.reasoning: Operation Sadbhavana is the Indian Army's long-running 'hearts and minds' initiative, addressing basic needs of people in remote and disturbed areas through schools, health care, infrastructure, vocational training and national-integration tours. The other three are quite different in character: Operation Sankalp is the naval maritime security deployment in the Gulf region, Operation Maitri was the earthquake relief and rescue mission in Nepal in 2015, and Operation Madad refers to flood relief assistance, notably in Kerala.

items.value: The Canada-United States border is the longest international border between any two countries
items.reasoning: The boundary between Canada and the United States runs to roughly 8,890 kilometres including the Alaska segment, which is the longest international border in the world. Kazakhstan-Russia, at around 7,600 kilometres, is the second longest and the longest continuous one, but still shorter. The Chile-Argentina border is about 5,300 kilometres and the China-India boundary shorter still and in any case undefined along much of its length.

items.value: Statements 1 and 3 only — the Ethics Committee began as an ad hoc body and cannot take up sub judice matters, but complaints are not confined to Members
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: the Ethics Committee of the Lok Sabha was first constituted in 2000 as an ad hoc committee and only later became a standing committee of the House. Statement 3 is correct: the Committee's own procedure bars it from entertaining a complaint on a matter that is sub judice. Statement 2 fails because of the word 'only' — a complaint of unethical conduct may be brought by any person, subject to its being forwarded through a Member and supported by evidence and an affidavit that it is not false, frivolous or vexatious; the requirement is a routing condition, not a restriction on who may complain. Runner-up is D, which would win if the examiner treats that routing requirement as meaning that in form only a Member of the Lok Sabha can make the complaint, in which case statement 2 would also be correct.

items.value: Statements 2 and 3 only — the reservation runs for fifteen years and includes a sub-quota for Scheduled Caste women, but does not take effect from the 18th Lok Sabha
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is incorrect: the Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act, 2023 provides that the reservation of seats for women shall take effect only after the relevant census has been published and a delimitation exercise carried out on its basis, so it does not apply to the Lok Sabha constituted in 2024. Statement 2 matches the Act's own text, which provides that the reservation shall cease to have effect on the expiry of fifteen years from the commencement of the Amendment Act, subject to extension by Parliament. Statement 3 is also in the Act: one-third of the seats already reserved for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes is reserved for women of those communities, that is a sub-quota within the existing quota. With 1 out and 3 in, only the combination 2 and 3 is available.

items.value: Statements 2, 3 and 4 — Mitra Shakti-2023 was held at Aundh in Pune, aimed at joint counter-terrorism response, and included the Air Force; but it is an India-Sri Lanka exercise, not India-Bangladesh
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is false and is the discriminating one: Mitra Shakti is the annual joint military exercise between India and Sri Lanka, whereas the India-Bangladesh series is Sampriti. Statement 2 is correct — the 2023 edition was conducted at the Aundh Military Station, Pune. Statement 3 is correct, the stated aim being interoperability in sub-conventional operations and a joint response in counter-terrorism under Chapter VII of the UN Charter. Statement 4 is correct, air force contingents from both sides taking part in the 2023 edition. Since statement 1 fails, the only option that excludes it is 2, 3 and 4.

items.value: A writ of Prohibition is issued to a lower court or tribunal to stop it continuing proceedings beyond its jurisdiction
items.reasoning: Prohibition lies only against judicial and quasi-judicial authorities and is preventive in nature: it is issued by a higher court to a lower court or tribunal forbidding it from continuing proceedings in a matter over which it has no jurisdiction or in which it is exceeding its jurisdiction. It is not available against an administrative officer acting in a non-judicial capacity, which rules out A and D, and it cannot be directed against a legislature at all, which rules out B. The remedy against a lower court's completed order is Certiorari, while Prohibition halts proceedings still under way.

items.value: Only statement 2 is correct — Scheduled Tribe status is State-specific, but it is the President and not the Governor who notifies a community as a Scheduled Tribe
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is incorrect: under Article 342(1) it is the President who, by public notification and after consultation with the Governor in the case of a State, specifies the tribes or tribal communities deemed to be Scheduled Tribes for that State, and under Article 342(2) only Parliament may thereafter include or exclude a community from that list. The Governor is consulted; he does not recognise or declare. Statement 2 is correct: the notification is made in relation to a particular State or Union territory, so a community listed as a Scheduled Tribe in one State need not be a Scheduled Tribe in another.

items.value: Only statement 2 is correct — no demand for a grant may be made except on the President's recommendation, but the Annual Financial Statement is laid on behalf of the President, not the Prime Minister
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is incorrect on a point of constitutional text: Article 112 requires the President to cause the Annual Financial Statement to be laid before both Houses, and the Finance Minister does so on behalf of the President — not on behalf of the Prime Minister. Statement 2 is correct and reproduces Article 113(3), which provides that no demand for a grant shall be made except on the recommendation of the President. So only 2 stands.

items.value: S. Jaishankar wrote both 'The India Way' and 'Why Bharat Matters'
items.reasoning: Both books are by Dr. Subrahmanyam Jaishankar, the External Affairs Minister — 'The India Way: Strategies for an Uncertain World' published in 2020 and 'Why Bharat Matters' in 2024. Shashi Tharoor's foreign-policy titles are quite different works such as 'Pax Indica'; Bhupender Yadav has co-authored a book on the Bharatiya Janata Party; and Nalin Mehta is the author of 'The New BJP'.

items.value: Only two pairs are correct — Argentina's economic crisis and the Sudanese army-versus-paramilitary war; Turkey has not left NATO
items.reasoning: Pair 1 is correct: Argentina has been in the news for a severe economic crisis marked by triple-digit inflation, currency collapse and drastic austerity measures. Pair 2 is correct: since April 2023 Sudan has been at war between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces. Pair 3 is false: Turkey remains a member of NATO and has in fact been in the news for the opposite reason, its ratification of Sweden's accession to the alliance. So exactly two pairs match.

items.value: Both statements are correct, and the pipeline's Red Sea-to-Mediterranean link is precisely what makes it a strategic route for Gulf oil moving to Europe
items.reasoning: Statement-II is correct: the SUMED, or Suez-Mediterranean, pipeline runs from Ain Sukhna on the Gulf of Suez to Sidi Kerir on the Mediterranean coast, so it does connect the Red Sea with the Mediterranean. Statement-I is correct on the same footing: it is the only alternative to the Suez Canal for moving Persian Gulf crude northwards to Europe, and it takes on critical importance whenever the Canal or the Bab-el-Mandeb approach is disrupted. The explanatory relation holds because it is exactly this geographic short-cut across the Egyptian isthmus, bypassing the long haul round Africa, that gives the pipeline its strategic character — so B is excluded. Runner-up is D, which would win if the examiner reads Statement-I strictly: SUMED carries crude oil only and no natural gas, so the words 'and natural gas' would make Statement-I incorrect while Statement-II stayed correct.

items.value: Both statements are correct — the Red Sea gets very little precipitation and receives no river inflow
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: the Red Sea basin is one of the most arid on earth, with average annual precipitation of only a few centimetres, falling mostly as brief winter showers. Statement 2 is correct in the sense intended: no perennial river drains into the Red Sea, which together with intense evaporation and a narrow, shallow connection to the Indian Ocean at Bab-el-Mandeb is why it is among the most saline open seas in the world. Runner-up is A, which would win if the examiner counts the ephemeral wadis that discharge into the sea after occasional storms as water entering from rivers, which would make the absolute wording of statement 2 too strong.

items.value: Power plants burning fossil fuels are the largest source of sulphur dioxide emissions
items.reasoning: The Environmental Protection Agency identifies the burning of fossil fuels by power plants and other industrial facilities as the largest source of sulphur dioxide in the atmosphere, sulphur being an impurity in coal and heavy fuel oil that oxidises on combustion. Smaller sources it lists separately include the extraction of metal from ore, and fuel burning by locomotives, ships and other vehicles and heavy equipment — each of which appears among the distractors here precisely because it is a genuine but secondary source.

items.value: Both statements are correct, and the run of military takeovers is what accounts for the region's instability
items.reasoning: Statement-I is correct: the Sahel has seen a sharply worsening security situation, with jihadist insurgency spreading across Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger and spilling towards the Gulf of Guinea states. Statement-II is correct: the region has had a succession of coups d'etat in recent years — Mali in 2020 and 2021, Chad and Guinea in 2021, Burkina Faso twice in 2022 and Niger in 2023. The explanation holds because a coup is itself political instability, and these takeovers directly deepened the security crisis by triggering the withdrawal of French and other partner forces, regional sanctions and the departure of the junta-led states from ECOWAS. Runner-up is B, which would win if the examiner treats the coups as a symptom rather than a cause — on that reading the insecurity was driven by jihadist violence and state weakness, and the takeovers followed from it rather than explaining it.

items.value: Statement-I is incorrect — India does import apples from the United States — while Statement-II is correct that GM food cannot be imported without the competent authority's approval
items.reasoning: Statement-I is false: American apples have long been sold in the Indian market, and the trade was very much in the news in 2023 when India withdrew the additional retaliatory duty it had imposed on US apples in 2019, after which imports picked up again. Statement-II is correct: India's food safety law requires prior approval of the competent authority for import of genetically modified food, and importers must furnish a non-GM or approved-GM certificate for the notified crops. Since Statement-I is wrong and Statement-II right, options A, B and C all fail.

items.value: Only statement 1 is correct — the Speaker shall not preside, but he retains the right to speak and to vote in the first instance
items.reasoning: Article 96(1) provides that while a resolution for the Speaker's removal is under consideration he shall not preside, though he is present, so statement 1 is correct. Article 96(2) then expressly gives him the right to speak in and otherwise take part in the proceedings, so statement 2 is wrong; and it entitles him to vote on such a resolution in the first instance, denying him only the casting vote in the case of an equality of votes, so statement 3 is wrong as it inverts the rule. Only statement 1 stands.

items.value: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — a bill pending in the Lok Sabha, and one passed by the Lok Sabha but pending in the Rajya Sabha, both lapse; a bill notified for a joint sitting does not
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: any bill pending in the Lok Sabha lapses on its dissolution. Statement 2 is correct as well: a bill passed by the Lok Sabha but still pending in the Rajya Sabha lapses, because it has not completed its passage through both Houses. Statement 3 is the exception and is therefore false — Article 108(5) provides that where the President has notified his intention to summon the Houses to a joint sitting, the bill does not lapse on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha, and the joint sitting may still be held. The correct combination is 1 and 2, which is printed at option B.

items.value: Statements 2 and 3 are correct — prorogation normally follows adjournment sine die but may be done while the House is in session, and dissolution is on ministerial advice save in exceptional circumstances; prorogation is not free of ministerial advice
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is incorrect: the President prorogues a House under Article 85(2)(a) but, like his other functions, does so on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers under Article 74 — in practice on the government's recommendation. Statement 2 is correct and reflects settled parliamentary practice: prorogation ordinarily follows adjournment of the House sine die, but there is no bar to the President proroguing a House that is in session. Statement 3 is correct: dissolution of the Lok Sabha is effected by the President, normally on the advice of the Council of Ministers, discretion arising only in exceptional situations such as where the ministry has lost its majority. The correct combination is 2 and 3, printed at option C.

items.value: Statement-I is correct that the European Parliament approved the Net-Zero Industry Act, but Statement-II misstates both the target year and the ambition
items.reasoning: Statement-I is correct: the European Parliament approved the Net-Zero Industry Act in 2024, following the provisional political agreement reached with the Council earlier that year. Statement-II is wrong on two counts. The European Union's legally binding climate-neutrality target is 2050, not 2040, the 2040 figure being an intermediate emissions-reduction milestone rather than the carbon-neutrality date. And the Act's aim is far more modest than developing all its own clean technology: it sets a benchmark that the Union's manufacturing capacity should meet at least about 40 per cent of its annual deployment needs in strategic net-zero technologies by 2030.

items.value: Statement-I is incorrect — Venezuela has neither recovered rapidly nor stemmed the exodus — while Statement-II is correct that it holds the world's largest oil reserves
items.reasoning: Statement-I is false on both limbs: Venezuela's economy remains deeply depressed after years of contraction and hyperinflation, and it is the source of one of the largest displacement crises in the world, with roughly seven to eight million people having left the country. Statement-II is correct: Venezuela holds the largest proven crude oil reserves of any country, of the order of 300 billion barrels, concentrated in the extra-heavy crude of the Orinoco Belt — reserves it has been unable to monetise because of underinvestment and sanctions, which is precisely why the two statements do not sit together as claimed.

items.value: All three are correct — the Centre funds the programme fully, cadastral maps are digitised, and Records of Rights are being transliterated into the scheduled languages
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme was converted into a Central Sector Scheme funded entirely by the Central Government with effect from 2016, having earlier been a centrally sponsored scheme with cost sharing. Statement 2 is correct, digitisation of cadastral maps being one of the programme's core components alongside computerisation of the Record of Rights and computerisation of the registration process. Statement 3 is correct as well: a transliteration initiative has been taken up to render Records of Rights from the local language into the languages recognised in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution. Runner-up is B (2 and 3 only), which would win if the examiner treats the programme as still cost-shared between the Centre and the States rather than fully centrally funded.

items.value: Only statement 2 is correct — private specialists may volunteer at government facilities, but the scheme is antenatal only and carries no six-month post-delivery component
items.reasoning: Statement 2 is correct: the Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan invites private-sector obstetricians, gynaecologists and radiologists to volunteer their services at nearby government health facilities on the fixed day. Statement 1 is incorrect because of its tail: the scheme guarantees a fixed-day, free, assured and quality antenatal check-up on the ninth of every month to pregnant women in their second and third trimesters, and stops there — the six-months-post-delivery entitlement belongs to a different initiative, Surakshit Matritva Aashwasan, which covers mothers up to six months after delivery and sick newborns. Runner-up is C, which would win if the examiner reads statement 1 generously as a loose description of maternal-health assurance rather than holding it to the antenatal scope of this particular scheme.

items.value: Statements 2 and 3 only — contribution is age-specific and the assured pension is Rs 3,000 a month from age 60; the entry age starts at 18, and family pension goes to the spouse alone
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is incorrect: the entry age band for the Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan is 18 to 40 years, not 21 to 40. Statement 2 is correct: the monthly contribution rises with the age of entry, from about Rs 55 at eighteen to Rs 200 at forty, and is matched rupee for rupee by the Central Government. Statement 3 is correct: the scheme assures a minimum pension of Rs 3,000 per month once the subscriber attains sixty. Statement 4 is incorrect: family pension under the scheme is confined to the spouse, who receives fifty per cent of the pension, and children including unmarried daughters are not entitled to it. The surviving combination is 2 and 3.
